newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso firms up at close on dollar inflow.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso firms up at close on dollar inflow.

text.p: The Mexican peso gathered strength towards the close after being mixed in earlier trade as traders stopped covering short dollar positions, traders said.
"Dollars are still trickling in, we just didn't notice this morning because brokers were covering shorts," a trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate closed 1.3 and 0.7 of a centavo firmer, respectively, at 7.7500/7.7520 and 7.7460/7.7490 per dollar.
Same-day peso contracts had earlier closed 0.85 of a centavo weaker at 7.7460/7.7495 per dollar.
The 48-hour peso closed the week two centavos firmer than the previous week.
Dealers said that once brokers had covered their shorts in the morning, they changed dollars into pesos to invest in the local money market over the weekend.
"Some local players went short on dollars into the weekend as they think the peso will continue to appreciate next week," another dealer said.
"A local bank stepped in to buy dollars this morning and then sold in the early afternoon due to the favorable outlook for employment figures," he added.
Mexican open unemployment in January was 4.5 percent, compared to 6.4 percent for the same month in 1996, the National Statistics Institute said shortly after the close of trade.
A Reuters survey of financial professionals in Mexico showed they had been expecting an average rate of 4.84 percent.
Falling unemployment is not generally seen as a sign of an overheating economy in Mexico, and fuelling pressure on interest rates and weakening the currency.
On the contrary, it tends to be seen as a welcome sign of recovery from a severe recession that began with the peso devaluation crisis of December 1994.
